title: Cover the rest.cjs and liferay/index.cjs domain methods, and add an opt-in DXP integration suite
body:
Follow-up to #133, which closed after lifting the adapters to 98.7%, the path profile to 95.7% and `baseGenerator` to 81.8%. Two modules named there remain thin, for a specific reason rather than by oversight.

## Current state

| Module | Statements | Functions |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/liferay/rest.cjs` | 26.4% | 22.4% |
| `src/liferay/index.cjs` | 30.8% | 50.3% |

Overall coverage is 65.9% against a 60% gate.

## Why they are still thin

Between them these files hold roughly 150 methods that are a path, an op label and a call to `httpCore`. Writing one test per method would add bulk rather than signal, because the riskiest property - that the path exists - is already checked statically on every CI run by `yarn validate:rest`, which now covers both the `PATH` profile and paths written inline in the source (#131, #144).

The facade delegation on both files is also already covered generically: `tests/liferayServiceDelegation.test.js` discovers all 162 forwarding methods from their prototypes and asserts same-name forwarding, argument pass-through and return propagation.

## What is actually uncovered

1. **Op labels.** Each call passes an op string used for logging, error reporting and soft-status handling. Nothing verifies a method passes the op its behaviour depends on. #146 found the consequence: `SOFT_STATUS_BY_OP` carried 404 tolerance for two ops nothing emits, and seven by-ERC ops that are emitted have no entry. `tests/rest.test.js` now asserts every configured op is reachable, but not that each method passes the right one.
2. **Response handling.** Unwrapping, `asItems`/`asCount` shaping, and the per-method 404-to-null behaviour that several by-ERC lookups implement themselves.
3. **Parameter construction.** Filters, paging and field selection assembled per method.

## Proposed action

- Table-driven tests over the domain methods asserting the op label and the response shaping, rather than one bespoke test per method.
- An opt-in integration suite, excluded from the normal CI gate, that can be pointed at a real DXP with credentials supplied out of band. Every test in the suite today runs against msw, which answers whatever URL it is given - so mock-based tests can never catch a wrong URL, a wrong op or a response shape the real API does not return. This is the only remaining way to exercise these paths against something real.
- Raise the coverage gate again once the work lands.
